items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: Of course I worked with Glenny also, you know, I hired Glenny on different jobs too, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah, he was an age of a man at the time. Of course I worked with Glenny also, you know, I hired Glenny on different jobs too, you know. I needed a band. So I said I played most of the old age I played with.
Well after Arnold had passed, who were some of those other bands that you just splattered around with and stuff?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: He's worked with him and Rene too, worked with both of the bands off and on, you know.

ctx.x: When you played with Chris or heard him play, who else was in the band, can you remember? Ooh. Anybody else at all? I know you had all of them, but some of them maybe.

One of, how do you call it? Even old Glenny had worked with him off and on too. Oh, Albert Glenny. He's worked with him and Rene too, worked with both of the bands off and on, you know. That's what they used to do. Alternate in other words, you know. And one had more work than the other, well they'd work with him and the fellow had the most work, they'd work with them. That's where they used to go at the time.
Who was the highest note man around here at that time?

items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: Glenny used to say that all the time.

ctx.x: Glenny used to say that all the time. Oh, no, no, no. He said his mother could hardly speak English, and she'd say, some fellow, she's waiting not to see you. Say, can't you get another bass player? Bosses, yeah. Let's see. Let's see. What have we got now? I think we've got pretty much everything in the rhythm section, haven't we?
Yeah, I think that's all. Yeah, piano.
